hero.title:
The AI trip planner
built for groups
hero.subtitle: Most AI planners write an itinerary for one person. Yours has to survive six opinions.

quickAnswer.heading: Quick answer
quickAnswer.body: An AI trip planner turns a plain-language brief — where, when, how long, what the group likes — into a day-by-day itinerary in seconds, so you start from a draft instead of a blank page. WePlanify does that and then hands the draft to your group: everyone can edit it, vote on what stays, and follow a shared budget. It is free, and invited friends don't need an account.

steps.title: Describe the trip in a sentence
steps.body: Where you're going, roughly when, and what the group is into. No form to fill in first.

steps.title: Get a day-by-day draft
steps.body: The AI proposes an itinerary with activities and a realistic pace — something concrete to react to, which is the whole point.

steps.title: Hand it to the group
steps.body: Everyone edits, comments and votes. The plan converges instead of sitting in one person's notes app.

groups.title: Why a group needs a different AI planner
groups.body: A solo AI planner optimises one person's taste. A group has to reconcile six of them, plus a budget nobody wants to bring up and three people who reply late. That's a coordination problem, not a generation problem. WePlanify treats the generated itinerary as a starting draft, then gives the group what it takes to settle it: polls to decide, a shared budget that tracks who paid what, and a plan everyone watches change in real time.

honest.title: What AI is good at here — and what it isn't
honest.body: AI is genuinely good at the blank page: a plausible route, a sensible pace, a shortlist for a city you've never visited. It's much weaker on anything it can't check — current opening hours, whether a restaurant seats nine, what the ferry costs this month. Treat the draft as a first pass to react to, confirm the bookings yourself, and let the group catch what the model got wrong.

items.q: Is the AI trip planner free?
items.a: Yes. Generating itineraries is part of the free plan — no per-trip limit, no credit card. Invited friends can join and edit without creating an account.

items.q: Can I change what the AI suggests?
items.a: Yes, and you're expected to. The generated itinerary is a normal editable plan: move days around, delete what doesn't fit, add your own stops. Nothing is locked.

items.q: Does it work for a group, not just one traveller?
items.a: That's what it's built for. Once the draft exists, the whole group can edit it, run polls to settle the disagreements, and follow a shared budget that works out who owes whom.

items.q: How is this different from asking ChatGPT for an itinerary?
items.a: A chat gives you text you then have to paste somewhere and coordinate by hand. Here the itinerary is a live plan your group edits together, votes on and attaches a budget to — and it's still there when someone changes their mind three weeks later.
